questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following does NOT form part of the large intestine:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Ileum (2 marks)
The ileum is the last section of the small intestine. The large intestine consists of the caecum, colon and rectum.

subQuestions.questionText: A feed with total digestible nutrients (TDN) of 72% and digestible protein (DP) of 8% will have digestible non-nitrogen substances (DNNS) of …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - 64% (2 marks)
DNNS = %TDN − %DP = 72% − 8% = 64%.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following feeds has the highest biological value:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Fish meal (2 marks)
Proteins of animal origin, such as fish meal, contain all the essential amino acids in the right proportions, so they have the highest biological value. Linseed meal, peanut oilcake meal and lucerne are plant proteins with a lower biological value.

subQuestions.questionText:
In farm animals the oesophagus is an extension of the pharynx at the back of the oral cavity and:
(i) It connects the mouth with the stomach
(ii) It is a passage for bolus from the mouth to the stomach
(iii) It is where the absorption process starts
(iv) It regulates the swallowing process
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
The oesophagus connects the mouth to the stomach, carries the bolus and controls swallowing (peristalsis). No absorption of nutrients takes place in the oesophagus, so statement (iii) is wrong.

subQuestions.questionText: A permanent intensive poultry housing system in which the floor is covered with straw or wood shavings:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Deep-litter (2 marks)
In the deep-litter system birds move freely on a floor covered with a deep layer of litter (straw or wood shavings). In battery cages birds are kept in wire cages; free-range birds have outdoor access.

subQuestions.questionText: The following method of handling farm animals applies specifically to sheep:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Catch animals as high as possible on their hind legs (2 marks)
Sheep are caught by grasping the hind leg high up (above the hock) to avoid injury. Neck clamps are used for cattle; prodders/whips and uncontrolled dogs stress the animals.

options.A: Work with animals using a neck clamp
options.B: Use random dogs to manage them
options.C: Catch animals as high as possible on their hind legs
options.D: Use a prodder or a whip

subQuestions.questionText: A carrier organism that is responsible for the transmission of the disease-causing agent:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Vector (2 marks)
A vector is a carrier organism (e.g. a tick or mosquito) that transmits a pathogen. The pathogen is the disease-causing agent itself.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following are measures to prevent the absorption of poison already ingested:
(i) Animals should be kept away from drinking water
(ii) Administering strong tea or activated charcoal
(iii) Providing feed loaded with additives
(iv) Dosing animals with sugar or glucose
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
Water is withheld so the poison is not dissolved and absorbed faster; activated charcoal / strong tea (tannins) bind the poison; sugar/glucose protects the liver and supplies energy. Providing feed with additives (iii) does not prevent absorption of a poison already eaten.

subQuestions.questionText: The following is a milk pathway from the point of production in the udder until it is released:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Alveolus → gland cistern → teat cistern → teat canal (2 marks)
Milk is made in the alveoli, drains through the ducts into the gland cistern, then into the teat cistern, and leaves through the teat canal.

options.A: Teat canal → gland cistern → teat cistern → alveolus
options.B: Alveolus → teat canal → gland cistern → teat cistern
options.C: Alveolus → gland cistern → teat cistern → teat canal
options.D: Gland cistern → teat cistern → alveolus → teat canal

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following about meiotic cell division during spermatogenesis is NOT correct:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Produces two identical diploid (2n) daughter cells from a parent cell (2 marks)
That describes mitosis. Meiosis is a reduction division that halves the chromosome number and forms four haploid (n) daughter cells from one parent cell.

options.A: Halves the chromosome number to form reproductive cells
options.B: Produces two identical diploid (2n) daughter cells from a parent cell
options.C: Also known as reduction cell division
options.D: Forms four haploid (n) daughter cells from a parent cell

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A. Write A only, B only, both A and B or none.
COLUMN A: A: Maltase; B: Insulin
COLUMN B: Secreted by the islets of Langerhans
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B only (2 marks)
Insulin is secreted by the islets of Langerhans (in the pancreas). Maltase is an enzyme secreted by the intestinal glands.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Cud; B: Chyme
COLUMN B: Regurgitated bolus inside the mouth
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A only (2 marks)
The cud is the regurgitated bolus of food that a ruminant chews again in its mouth. Chyme is the semi-liquid, partly digested food in the stomach.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Poor meat quality; B: Aggressive temperament
COLUMN B: Consequence of the correct and frequent handling of animals
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
Correct and frequent handling produces calm, tame animals and good meat quality. Poor meat quality and aggressive temperament are consequences of incorrect or rough handling.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Export ban; B: Import ban
COLUMN B: Animals and their products are not allowed to enter or leave the country to control the spread of diseases
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
An export ban stops animals/products leaving the country and an import ban stops them entering; both are used to control the spread of disease.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Copulation; B: Courtship
COLUMN B: Involuntary contractions of the pelvic floor in male animals resulting in the discharge of semen
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
Involuntary contractions of the pelvic floor that discharge semen is ejaculation. Copulation is the physical act of mating; courtship is the behaviour before mating.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The collective name for the finger-like protrusions in the rumen of farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Papillae (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The farming system where the farmer raises pigs with the aim of feeding the family.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Subsistence (farming) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The type of cloning performed to produce embryonic stem cells that develop into new tissues and organs.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Therapeutic (cloning) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
A sixteen-celled solid ball that forms after fertilisation.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Morula (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The tube that transports sperm cells from the epididymis to the urethra.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Vas deferens / sperm duct / ductus deferens (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Mastication involves transportation of water and nutrient molecules from the small intestine into the blood stream.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Absorption (1 mark)
Absorption is the movement of digested nutrients and water from the small intestine into the blood. Mastication is chewing.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The blue tick is a three-host tick that transmits heartwater in farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Bont (tick) (1 mark)
The bont tick is a three-host tick and the vector of heartwater. The blue tick is a one-host tick that transmits redwater and gallsickness.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The allantois brings blood of the mother and foetus in close contact.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Placenta (1 mark)
The placenta is the organ that brings the maternal and foetal blood supplies into close contact for the exchange of nutrients, gases and wastes.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Ovum transfer occurs when the nucleus of a body cell is transferred to an enucleated unfertilised egg cell.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Nuclear transfer / cloning (1 mark)
Transferring the nucleus of a body cell into an enucleated egg cell is nuclear transfer (cloning).

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
A Graafian follicle develops in the ovary after ovulation in the place of the burst follicle.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Corpus luteum (1 mark)
After ovulation the corpus luteum (yellow body) develops in the place of the burst follicle and secretes progesterone.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents the alimentary canal of a farm animal, with the associated organs shown: A is the large lobed organ at the front; the gall bladder is labelled beneath it; B is the elongated glandular organ lying in the loop of the first part of the small intestine; C is the coiled small intestine.
Identify, in the diagram above, the parts labelled A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Liver (1 mark)
B - Pancreas (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO functions of an alkaline substance (bile) secreted in A (the liver).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Activates the enzyme lipase to break down fats
• Emulsifies fats (breaks large fat globules into small droplets)
• Improves the absorption of fatty acids and glycerol
• Helps with the absorption of the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, K and E
• Is antiseptic and therefore counteracts putrefaction
• Neutralises the acidic chyme coming from the stomach

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE intestinal gland located in part C (the small intestine).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Gland / crypts of Lieberkühn
• Brunner's glands / duodenal glands

subQuestions.questionText:
There is a relationship between the micro-organisms and the digestion of roughages.
State TWO requirements for the normal functioning of micro-organisms in the rumen of cattle.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Anaerobic conditions / oxygen-free environment
• Presence of carbon dioxide
• A pH of 5,5–6,5 / slightly acidic
• A temperature of 38–42 °C / warm environment
• Regular intake of food
• Removal of waste products
• Correct osmotic conditions / presence of moisture
• Presence of volatile fatty acids
• Sufficient nutrients / minerals
• Easily digestible carbohydrates

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE function of the micro-organisms in the rumen of cattle.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Digestion of cellulose / hemicellulose
• Hydrolysis of proteins
• Synthesis of vitamins
• Synthesis of amino acids

subQuestions.questionText: Name the type of micro-organism that forms the least in terms of population in the rumen of cattle.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): Fungi; Viruses; Archaea

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagrams in the question paper illustrate the processes of food absorption into the bloodstream of farm animals. DIAGRAM A shows many particles moving through the cell membrane in the direction of an arrow, from where they are crowded to where they are few. DIAGRAM B shows a carrier protein in the membrane moving particles from where they are few to where they are many, powered by ATP.
Identify the type of food absorption illustrated in:
(a) DIAGRAM A
(b) DIAGRAM B
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) DIAGRAM A - Passive absorption / diffusion / osmosis (1 mark)
(b) DIAGRAM B - Active absorption (active transport) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the diagram (A or B) that represents the process responsible for the absorption of glucose and certain amino acids.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Diagram B (1 mark)
Glucose and certain amino acids are absorbed by active transport.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the absorption process in DIAGRAM B.
subQuestions.memoText: Absorption of nutrients from a low to a high concentration / against the concentration gradient ✓, with the aid of ATP as a source of energy ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
The nutrient components of two different feeds are shown below:
FEED A: Digestible protein 7%; Total digestible nutrients 58%; Crude fibre content 21%
FEED B: Digestible protein 16%; Total digestible nutrients 82%; Crude fibre content 8%
Classify the following:
(a) FEED A
(b) FEED B
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) FEED A - Roughage (1 mark)
(b) FEED B - Concentrate (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Justify the classification of FEED B in QUESTION 2.4.1, based on the data provided above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• It has a high protein content / 16%
• It has a high total digestible nutrient content / TDN 82%
• It has a low crude fibre content / 8%

subQuestions.questionText: Name the farm animal that is unable to digest FEED A.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pig / fowl / poultry (a non-ruminant, which cannot digest the high crude fibre content) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the feed that is suitable for EACH of the following:
(a) Improves the functioning of the digestive system in ruminant farm animals
(b) Stimulates production of more butterfat in milk
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Feed A (roughage) (1 mark)
(b) Feed A (roughage) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The schematic representation in the question paper illustrates the nutrient composition of a feed for farm animals: FEED (30 kg) splits into DRY MATTER (25 kg) and A; DRY MATTER splits into B and C; C splits into PROTEIN and D; D leads to FATS & OILS.
Label nutrient component C.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Organic component(s) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the value for component A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: 5 kg (1 mark)
A represents water: 30 kg feed − 25 kg dry matter = 5 kg.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the digestibility coefficient of the feed using the data in the schematic representation above, assuming that the animal excreted 6 kg dry material. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – Formula: DC = [(Dry material intake − Dry material excreted) ÷ Dry material intake] × 100 ✓ (1 mark)
Step 2 – Substitution: = [(25 kg − 6 kg) ÷ 25 kg] × 100 ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – Answer: = 76% ✓✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
The schematic representation in the question paper indicates the energy flow of maize meal that was fed to a pregnant farm animal: Gross energy (37,2 MJ) → A [faecal energy lost = 9,8 MJ] → C [gases and (B) energy lost = 4 MJ] → E [heat production = (D)].
Define the energy represented by A.
subQuestions.memoText: Digestible energy is the gross energy ✓ minus the energy lost in the faeces ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Label B.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Urine (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE function of the energy represented by E.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): For maintenance / production / reproduction / growth / work

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the value of the energy represented by C. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText: Metabolic energy (C) = 37,2 MJ − 9,8 MJ − 4 MJ ✓ = 23,4 MJ ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
A farmer mixed 15 parts of FEED A with 5 parts of FEED B to get a ration with 16% digestible protein.
Calculate (in kg) the quantity of FEED B required in a 750 kg ration. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – Total parts = 15 + 5 = 20 parts ✓ (1 mark)
Step 2 – FEED B (kg) = (5 ÷ 20) × 750 kg ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – Answer = 187,5 kg ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The picture in the question paper shows a production system: a large number of dairy cattle held on a small area of pasture next to a big barn with feed silos.
Identify the production system shown in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Intensive production system (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for the answer to QUESTION 3.1.1 by referring to the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• A large number of animals on a small area of land / high stocking density
• The presence of housing structures / facilities / silos
• More capital has been invested (buildings, equipment)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper show two facilities used under different environmental conditions. PICTURE A is an open-sided, raised structure with only a roof (an open shade shelter). PICTURE B is a closed barn in which calves are kept in pens on a floor covered with a layer of bedding material.
Identify the picture of the facility that is used under EACH of the following environmental conditions:
(a) Very cold and windy conditions
(b) Hot summer conditions
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Very cold and windy conditions - PICTURE B (1 mark)
(b) Hot summer conditions - PICTURE A (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the term for the material that covers the floor in PICTURE B, which will act as an insulator.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Bedding (litter) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Below is a list of structures, tools and apparatus used to handle and manage farm animals:
A: Barbed wire fence to demarcate an area of farmland
B: A separate crush
C: Red flags and warning signs
D: Kraal made of branches
E: Shelter made of poles and canvas
Choose, from the list above, the structure, tool or apparatus applicable to the statement below. Write down only the letter (A–E).
For implementation of a rotational grazing system.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: A (a barbed wire fence to demarcate the grazing camps) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose, from the list (A: Barbed wire fence to demarcate an area of farmland; B: A separate crush; C: Red flags and warning signs; D: Kraal made of branches; E: Shelter made of poles and canvas), the structure, tool or apparatus applicable to the statement below. Write down only the letter.
Used by subsistence farmers to house farm animals overnight.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: D (a kraal made of branches) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose, from the list (A: Barbed wire fence to demarcate an area of farmland; B: A separate crush; C: Red flags and warning signs; D: Kraal made of branches; E: Shelter made of poles and canvas), the structure, tool or apparatus applicable to the statement below. Write down only the letter.
Alerting road users about farm animals crossing a public road.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: C (red flags and warning signs) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the body temperature, number of breaths and number of heartbeats per minute of different farm animals:
Horse: Body temperature 38 °C; Breaths 12; Heartbeats 40
Cattle: Body temperature 39 °C; Breaths 25; Heartbeats 65
Sheep: Body temperature 40 °C; Breaths 16; Heartbeats 75
Goat: Body temperature 41 °C; Breaths 16; Heartbeats 75
Pig: Body temperature 40 °C; Breaths 14; Heartbeats 70
Draw a combined bar graph showing the body temperatures and the number of heartbeats of the different farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
A combined (double) bar graph of body temperature and heartbeat for each farm animal.

MARKING CRITERIA (1 mark each):
• Correct heading (naming both variables, e.g. 'The body temperature and heartbeat of the different farm animals')
• X-axis: correctly calibrated with label (Farm animals)
• Y-axis: correctly calibrated with label (Body temperature and heartbeat)
• Correct units (°C and per minute)
• Combined bar graph (the two bars grouped per animal, with a key)
• Accuracy (at least 80% of bars correctly plotted)

Values to plot:
• Horse: temperature 38; heartbeat 40
• Cattle: temperature 39; heartbeat 65
• Sheep: temperature 40; heartbeat 75
• Goat: temperature 41; heartbeat 75
• Pig: temperature 40; heartbeat 70

subQuestions.questionText:
Name a method that is used to administer the type of medication listed below:
Liquid medicine given orally to a farm animal.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Dosing / drenching (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name a method that is used to administer the type of medication listed below:
Inserting medication into the muscle of a farm animal.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Injecting (intramuscular injection) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Complete the table below by writing down ONLY the missing information for A, B, C, D and E.
Row 1 - Disease: Ringworm; Pathogen: A; Main symptoms: Round, scaly patches of hairless skin
Row 2 - Disease: B; Pathogen: Virus; Main symptoms: High fever, blotchy lesions, diarrhoea, abortion, nasal discharge, coughing, difficulty breathing
Row 3 - Disease: Mastitis; Pathogen: Bacteria; Main symptoms: C
Row 4 - Disease: Redwater; Pathogen: D; Main symptoms: Acute abdominal pain, anaemia and dark to brown urine
Row 5 - Disease: E; Pathogen: Bacteria; Main symptoms: High fever, swelling of the body, bloody discharge from mouth, nose and rectum
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Fungus (1 mark)
B - African swine fever / swine flu (1 mark)
C - Inflammation of the udder / the milk is thick, watery and flaky / a drop in milk production / reduced mobility due to limping (1 mark)
D - Protozoa (1 mark)
E - Anthrax (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below illustrates the life stages of parasites.
PARASITE A: Eggs in faeces → Embryo in intestines → Scolex in intestines → Adult parasite
PARASITE B: Eggs hatch in water → Larvae in snail → Parasite attach to grass → Cattle eat grass → Parasite in the livers of cattle
Classify the parasites illustrated by the life stages above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Internal parasites / endoparasites (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name parasite A.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Tapeworm (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Classify parasite B based on the number of hosts to complete the life cycle.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Two-host parasite (1 mark)
Parasite B uses a snail as an intermediate host and cattle as the final host.

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO costs associated with the control of the parasites illustrated in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Treatment costs / the cost of anthelmintics (dewormers) (1 mark)
• Labour costs at the time of treatment (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper show parasites that are harmful to farm animals: PARASITE A is a fly with a stout body and one pair of wings (a blowfly / housefly); PARASITE B is described as microscopic and is drawn as a rounded, eight-legged organism (a mite).
Identify the parasite (A or B) above that matches the descriptions below:
(a) Causes scab and mange in animals
(b) Lays eggs in an area soaked in urine and faeces, and infests open wounds in wool sheep
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Parasite B (mite) (1 mark)
(b) Parasite A (blowfly) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO symptoms of a PARASITE B (mite) infestation in farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Skin irritation
• Dermatitis / inflammation of the skin
• Hair (wool) loss
• Restlessness
• Biting / rubbing / kicking / wagging of the tail to relieve the discomfort
• Skin breaks (wounds)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO precautionary measures to take to prevent the infestation of PARASITE A (blowfly).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Correct timing of shearing and crutching
• Lambing time should be after shearing
• Clipping and cleaning of the coat
• Breeding resistant animals
• Tail docking
• Sanitation / hygienic practices
• Proper treatment of wounds

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the type of parasite that is treated using the following method:
Administering anthelmintics to farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Internal parasite / endoparasite (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the type of parasite that is treated using the following method:
Applying a toxic solution to the body of the animal.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: External parasite / ectoparasite (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper shows the reproductive process in farm animals. On the left is the ovary, with 'oocyte maturation' labelled and a small round cell labelled A. In the oviduct, a point of 'early embryonic development' is shown and a tadpole-shaped cell is labelled B. The oviduct, uterus (with a foetus) and testes are all labelled. Number 1 points to the ovary and number 2 points to a point in the oviduct.
Identify A and B in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Egg cell / ovum / female gamete (1 mark)
B - Sperm cell / male gamete / spermatozoon (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the process through which B (the sperm cell) is produced.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Spermatogenesis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example of a secondary female reproductive organ visible in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): Uterus; Fallopian tube / oviduct; Infundibulum

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the reproductive processes taking place at 1 and 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
1 - Ovulation (1 mark)
2 - Fertilisation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE function of EACH of the following organs:
(a) Fallopian tube
(b) Uterus
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Fallopian tube - any ONE (1 mark):
• Site for fertilisation
• Transports the sperm cells and egg cell in opposite directions
• Transports the zygote to the uterine body

(b) Uterus - any ONE (1 mark):
• For implantation of the developing embryo
• Protects and nourishes the embryo
• Contraction of the uterine walls to facilitate fertilisation and expulsion of the foetus
• Houses the embryo / foetus

subQuestions.questionText:
Farmers usually manipulate the reproductive process in female farm animals so that they can come on heat at the same time.
Name the reproductive process described above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Oestrus synchronisation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate ONE method that farmers can use to ensure that the process named in QUESTION 4.2.1 is a success.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Injecting prostaglandin / administering FSH or LH
• Implants containing progesterone
• Injecting stilboestrol / oestrogen
• Mixing MGA / a progestagen in the feed
• Inserting a controlled internal drug release (CIDR) device into the vagina
• Administering gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the factor causing sterility and infertility in bulls associated with each of the following:
(a) Bull has an unbalanced ration
(b) Young bull is raised in isolation
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Bull has an unbalanced ration - Malnutrition (1 mark)
(b) Young bull is raised in isolation - Inexperience / immaturity (lack of learned mating behaviour) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The illustration in the question paper represents a reproductive process that takes place in a female farm animal, shown as four stages A, B, C and D:
A: Lasts 12–15 days; the corpus luteum remains to maintain high levels of progesterone
B: Lasts 3 days; oestrogen is at its lowest levels
C: Lasts 2–3 days; FSH stimulates the development of follicles
D: Lasts 12–18 hours; oestrogen increases to high levels
Identify the process illustrated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: The oestrus cycle (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify stages C and D of the process in QUESTION 4.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
C - Pro-oestrus (1 mark)
D - Oestrus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE practical method that dairy farmers can use to identify cows on heat.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Use of a pedometer
• Use of tail chalking
• Use of chin-ball markers
• Use of heat mount detectors / KaMaR heat detectors
• Use of teaser animals
• Regular observation / close monitoring of heat behaviour

subQuestions.questionText:
The demonstration in the question paper shows a reproductive technique used by farmers to increase animal production, in stages 1 to 7: (1) best bull with desired traits; (2) semen is collected from the bull; (3) semen is collected into a tube; (4) semen stored in a liquid nitrogen tank (straws A, B, C); (5) straws thawed in a thermos flask; (6) semen straws; (7) a technician places a pistolette (insemination gun) into the best cow.
Identify the reproductive technique in stage 7 above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Artificial insemination / AI (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the method of collection in stage 2 of the technique demonstrated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Use of an artificial vagina (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Collected semen is mixed with a diluant made up of egg yolk, milk, glycerol, buffers and antibiotics.
Give the role of EACH of the following substances in a diluant:
(a) Antibiotics
(b) Buffers
(c) Egg yolk
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Antibiotics - prevent bacterial growth / infections in the semen (1 mark)
(b) Buffers - protect the sperm against changes in pH (1 mark)
(c) Egg yolk - provides nutrients for the sperm cells / prevents cold shock (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper illustrates a reproductive technique in female farm animals: embryos are collected from Female 1 (a black-and-white cow) and are then transferred, one each, into Female 2, Female 3 and Female 4.
Define the technique illustrated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Embryo transfer is a technique in which embryos are harvested (flushed) from the donor cow ✓ and transferred into recipient cows ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give the term referring to EACH of the following farm animals:
(a) Female 1
(b) Females 2, 3 and 4
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Female 1 - Donor / superior cow (1 mark)
(b) Females 2, 3 and 4 - Recipient / inferior / surrogate cows (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the importance of Female 1 in the technique above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: It provides genetically superior characteristics / embryos (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE disadvantage of the technique defined in QUESTION 4.5.1 for the farmer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• It is expensive
• Requires skills and experience
• Synchronisation of the recipient and donor is difficult
• The donor cow may not become pregnant after being artificially inseminated
• Time consuming and labour intensive
• Recipient cows may not become pregnant / abortion may occur
• An embryo from a superior cow does not necessarily guarantee a superior calf

subQuestions.questionText:
Statements that apply during parturition are given below:
A: The uterus contracts to expel the placenta.
B: Vagina, cervix and uterus enlarged to form a common canal.
C: Cow lies down, head and front legs of the foetus emerge from the vulva.
D: Foetus lies with front feet pointing towards the cervix with chin resting on the front legs.
Rearrange the statements above in the correct sequence. Write only the letter (A–D).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct sequence (1 mark for each letter in the correct position):
D – B – C – A
(The foetus positions itself; the birth canal opens up; the calf is expelled; then the placenta is expelled.)

subQuestions.questionText:
Milk synthesis and milk ejection in a cow are controlled by the hormones prolactin and oxytocin respectively. Milk ejection is initiated by stimulation of the central nervous system. Milk synthesis takes 305 days after which a cow dries off before the next parturition.
State ONE method in which the milker can stimulate the milk let-down process.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Washing the udder with warm water
• Massaging the udder
• Bringing the calf closer to the cow
• Making sounds (e.g. whistling)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate how oxytocin stimulates the milk let-down process.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: It causes contraction of the myoepithelial cells surrounding the alveoli, forcing milk out into the ducts (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the importance of a dry period for a lactating cow.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: To give the glandular (secretory) tissues of the udder time to rest and recover before the next lactation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the substance in the colostrum that provides the calf with immunity against diseases.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Antibodies / immunoglobulins (1 mark)
